text: Implement a system-wide dark theme by default with a light mode toggle. This choice enhances visibility and reduces eye strain in low-light environments, aligning with user preferences for modern interfaces. name: Pane
text: Pane: The real risk isn’t just extra design work—it’s that the light mode toggle becomes a crutch for poor dark theme execution. A better alternative: enforce dark theme by default but let users override it permanently, not toggle it. Settle this by testing both options with users—if the toggle gets flipped back to light mode more than 30% of the time, we’ve failed.

name: Facet
text:
We should enforce a dark theme by default and allow users to override it permanently, as this approach promotes a consistent and well-designed dark theme experience. By doing so, we accept the trade-off of potentially alienating a small subset of users who strongly prefer a light theme, but this is outweighed by the benefits of a cohesive and visually appealing interface. This decision also reduces the complexity associated with maintaining a toggle switch, allowing us to focus on refining the dark theme. By making this choice, we prioritize a high-quality, dark-themed interface that aligns with modern design trends and user expectations.
